## formal
Let $e_{1}, e_{2}, e_{3}$ be an orthonormal basis generating $\Cl(3,0)$, $p = \tfrac12(1 + e_{3})$, and $S = \Cl(3,0)\,p$, a left ideal of dimension four (a module of least dimension, \claimref{std-algebra.periodicity}), with the positive definite product $\langle \tilde\psi\varphi \rangle_{0}$. For $x = x_{1}e_{1} + x_{2}e_{2} + x_{3}e_{3}$ let $g(x)\psi = x\psi$ and $G_{x}(\psi, \varphi) = \langle \tilde\psi\, x\, \varphi \rangle_{0}$: multiplication by the position vector, the family of clause (8) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.strict-completions-exist-exactly-when-the-signature-does-not-jump} for $m = 3$ on the least module. It is symmetric, $g(x)^{2} = Q(x)$, so it degenerates at the origin only and has signature $(2,2)$ elsewhere. For $k \geq 1$ let $S^{(k)}$ be the orthogonal sum of $k$ copies of $S$ with the same action. Over the unit sphere let $\pi(x) = \tfrac12(1 + x)$ and $G_{+} = \{(x, \psi) : x\psi = \psi\} = \pi(x)S$, the positive eigenbundle, of rank two; $G_{-}$ is defined with $-x$. A bundle is \emph{stably trivial} if its sum with some trivial bundle is trivial. Completions, strict completions and model completions (a fixed exterior form $K_{0}$ on a fixed space $W_{0}$) are those of the cited Theorem.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)] \emph{(Frames and clutching function.)} $n_{1} = \pi(x)\,p$ and $n_{2} = \pi(x)\,e_{1}e_{2}\,p$ are orthogonal of square $\tfrac14(1 + x_{3})$, a frame of $G_{+}$ where $x_{3} > -1$; $s_{1} = \pi(x)\,e_{1}p$ and $s_{2} = \pi(x)\,e_{2}p$ are orthogonal of square $\tfrac14(1 - x_{3})$, a frame where $x_{3} < 1$. On the equator $x = \cos a\,e_{1} + \sin a\,e_{2}$,
\[
s_{1} = \cos a\; n_{1} - \sin a\; n_{2}, \qquad s_{2} = \sin a\; n_{1} + \cos a\; n_{2} :
\]
the second frame is the first turned through the angle of the point, one full turn round the equator.
\item[(2)] \emph{(Rotor lift.)} In the Clifford algebra of the fibre of $G_{+} \oplus \underline{\R}^{N}$, $N \geq 0$, with $f_{1}, f_{2}$ the unit vectors along $n_{1}, n_{2}$, the turn of (1) is $v \mapsto R_{a}v\tilde R_{a}$ with $R_{a} = \cos\tfrac a2 + \sin\tfrac a2\, f_{1}f_{2}$, which fixes the added directions; $R_{0} = 1$ and $R_{2\pi} = -1$. For $S^{(k)}$ the clutching function is the same turn in $k$ orthogonal planes and its rotor, the product of the $k$ plane rotors, ends at $(-1)^{k}$.
\item[(L)] \emph{(Lifting through the double cover.)} The \emph{rotors} of $\Cl(n,0)$ are the even versors of unit vectors, the group $\Spin(n,0) = \Spin^{+}(n,0)$ of Definition \claimref{obj.std-algebra.pin-spin} (in definite signature every unit vector has square one, so $R\tilde R = 1$ for each of them and $\mathrm{SO}^{+} = \mathrm{SO}$). Let $n \geq 1$ and let $\kappa \colon [0,1] \times [0,1] \to \mathrm{SO}(n)$ be continuous with $\kappa(u,0) = \kappa(u,1)$ for every $u$ and $\kappa(1,t)$ independent of $t$: a loop of rotations contracted through loops. Then there is a continuous map $\hat\kappa$ of the square into the rotors with $\hat\kappa(u,t)\,v\,\hat\kappa(u,t)^{\sim} = \kappa(u,t)v$ for all vectors $v$, $\hat\kappa(u,0) = \hat\kappa(u,1)$ for every $u$ and $\hat\kappa(1,t)$ independent of $t$; and every continuous path of rotors over $\kappa(0,\cdot)$ is $\hat\kappa(0,\cdot)$ or $-\hat\kappa(0,\cdot)$, so it is closed.
\item[(3)] \emph{(Not stably trivial.)} For $k$ odd, in particular on the least module, neither eigenbundle of the family on $S^{(k)}$ is stably trivial over the sphere: $G_{\pm} \oplus \underline{\R}^{N}$ is not trivial for any $N \geq 0$.
\item[(4)] \emph{(Completions, $k$ odd.)} Let $U \subset \R^{3}$ be a bounded open set containing the origin. For $k$ odd, no model completion of the family on $S^{(k)}$ standard outside $U$, with any $W_{0}$ and any $K_{0}$, is nondegenerate at every point. Strict completions exist (the double of the cited Theorem); the eigenbundles of their exterior form $K = -G$ are those of $G$ exchanged, so they carry the class, as the transfer clause requires.
\item[(5)] \emph{(Completions, $k$ even.)} Let $p_{4} = \tfrac12(1 + e_{1}e_{2}e_{3}e_{4})$ in $\Cl(4,0)$ and $T = \Cl(4,0)\,p_{4}$, of dimension eight. Under $\Cl(3,0)$, $T = S\,p_{4} \oplus S\,e_{1}p_{4}$, two orthogonal copies of $S$ (each map $s \mapsto s\,p_{4}$, $s \mapsto s\,e_{1}p_{4}$ commutes with left multiplication and halves the product), and left multiplication by $e_{4}$ is a fourth symmetric map of square one anticommuting with $e_{1}, e_{2}, e_{3}$. So on $S^{(2)} \cong T$, and on $S^{(k)}$ for every even $k$, the family $x + \beta e_{4}$, with $\beta$ continuous, positive at the origin and zero outside $U$, is nondegenerate at every point: a model completion with no added direction, and both eigenbundles are trivial over the sphere.
\item[(6)] \emph{(Summary.)} For the position vector of $\R^{3}$ on a sum of $k$ copies of the least module, a model completion standard outside a bounded neighbourhood of the origin and nondegenerate everywhere exists if and only if $k$ is even. The obstruction is the sign $(-1)^{k}$ at which the rotor lift of the clutching function ends. In the group of stable classes of real vector bundles over the two-sphere (bundles up to the addition of trivial bundles, under direct sum) the class of $G_{+}$ on the least module has order exactly two: it is not zero by (3), and twice it is the class of $G_{+}$ on $S^{(2)}$, which is zero by (5). It is a class of degree two: it is not seen on any circle of the sphere, the circle bounding a disc over which $G_{+}$ is trivial. On $S$ itself, (4) with $W_{0} = 0$ rules out every repair on the same module, of whatever form; the computation that no nonzero symmetric map anticommutes with $e_{1}, e_{2}, e_{3}$ shows only the special case that no repair of the form $x + \beta E$ of clause (8) of the cited Theorem exists.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Reading.} With the cases $m = 1$ and $m = 2$ of the cited Theorem this proves, for the least modules of $\Cl(m,0)$ with $m = 1, 2, 3$, that the degeneration of the position vector at its zero divisor cannot be removed by a completion with a fixed exterior form, and for $m = 3$ that it is removed on exactly the even multiples of the least module. The codimensions $m \equiv 1, 2, 3, 5 \pmod 8$ beyond $m = 3$ remain as cited there (the periodicity theorem of Bott in the form of Atiyah, Bott and Shapiro, from memory, not used here). That the sign of (6) is the second Stiefel-Whitney class of the eigenbundle, and that it is the whole stable class of a bundle over the two-sphere, are classical statements cited from memory and not used.

## technical
For the position vector of $\R^{3}$ acting by left multiplication on $S = \Cl(3,0)\tfrac12(1 + e_{3})$, the least module, and on sums $S^{(k)}$ of $k$ copies:

(1) the positive eigenbundle over the unit sphere is $\pi(x)S$, $\pi(x) = \tfrac12(1 + x)$, with frames $\pi(x)p$, $\pi(x)e_{1}e_{2}p$ away from the south pole and $\pi(x)e_{1}p$, $\pi(x)e_{2}p$ away from the north pole; on the equator the second is the first turned through the angle of the point, one full turn;

(2) the rotor of that turn, $\cos\tfrac a2 + \sin\tfrac a2 f_{1}f_{2}$, runs from $1$ to $-1$, and to $(-1)^{k}$ on $S^{(k)}$, whatever trivial directions are added;

(3) a bundle that becomes trivial after adding directions has a contractible clutching loop of rotations, and a loop of rotations contracted through loops lifts to closed loops of rotors (clause (L), proved from the stored double cover, the stored centre and compactness); so for $k$ odd the eigenbundles are not stably trivial;

(4) hence, by the stored transfer clause, for $k$ odd no completion with a fixed exterior form is nondegenerate everywhere, with any added directions;

(5) for $k$ even the module is a sum of copies of the least module of $\Cl(4,0)$, on which $e_{4}$ repairs the family with no added direction.

A completion with a fixed exterior form exists iff $k$ is even: in the group of stable classes of real vector bundles over the two-sphere, the eigenbundle class of the isolated degeneration in codimension three on the least module has order two, and it is read off as the sign at which the rotor lift ends.

Ledger: transport-convenient. The statement is the classical nontriviality of the generator of the real K-group of the two-sphere (prior art: Atiyah, Bott and Shapiro 1964, from memory), proved here without characteristic classes, by the rotor of the full turn, and read on the series' object: division by a vector fails at the zero divisor $x = 0$, and in three dimensions the failure cannot be repaired by adjoining flat directions with a fixed form, only by doubling the module.

## lay
Multiplying by a position vector can be undone by dividing by it, except at the origin, where the vector is zero. An earlier result asked whether this failure of division at one point can be repaired by enlarging the space the multiplication acts on, in a way that looks the same in every direction far from the point. In one and two dimensions it cannot. In three dimensions the answer was only quoted from the literature.

This result proves it for three dimensions, by a direct computation. On a sphere around the origin the multiplication has a space of vectors that it leaves unchanged, and that space turns as the point moves over the sphere. Comparing its description on the northern and southern halves, one finds that along the equator the two differ by one full turn. A full turn is the motion that returns every vector to itself but reverses the sign of a rotor, the object that generates rotations in the algebra. That sign survives the addition of any number of further fixed directions, and it is what blocks the repair.

Two copies of the multiplication side by side make two full turns, the signs cancel, and the repair exists: it is the multiplication by a vector of four dimensions, restricted to three. So in three dimensions the failure of division at the origin carries a twist that can be cancelled only in pairs.

## one-liner
For the position vector of $\R^{3}$ on $k$ copies of the least module of $\Cl(3,0)$, the clutching function of the positive eigenbundle is one full turn in $k$ planes, its rotor lift ends at $(-1)^{k}$, so for $k$ odd the eigenbundles are not stably trivial and no completion with a fixed exterior form is nondegenerate everywhere, while for $k$ even the fourth generator of $\Cl(4,0)$ repairs the family with no added direction: a class of order two, in the group of stable classes of bundles over the two-sphere, and of degree two.

proofs.proof-main.tex:
\emph{Setting.} For a vector $x$, $\tilde x = x$, so $\langle (x\psi)^{\sim}\varphi \rangle_{0} = \langle \tilde\psi\,x\,\varphi \rangle_{0}$: left multiplication by $x$ is symmetric for the product, and $g(x)^{2}\psi = x^{2}\psi = Q(x)\psi$. For a unit vector $x$ it is an involution with eigenspaces $\pi(\pm x)S$, where $\pi(x) = \tfrac12(1 + x)$ satisfies $\pi^{2} = \pi = \tilde\pi$ and $x\pi = \pi x = \pi$; a unit vector orthogonal to $x$ anticommutes with $x$ and exchanges the two eigenspaces, so each has dimension two and $G_{x}$ has signature $(2,2)$ for $x \neq 0$. The product is positive definite on $S$ (computed: the four elements $p$, $e_{1}p$, $e_{2}p$, $e_{1}e_{2}p$ are orthogonal of square $\tfrac12$). By the table of \claimref{std-algebra.periodicity}, $\Cl(3,0)$, of dimension eight, is the algebra of $2 \times 2$ matrices over a division algebra of real dimension two, whose least module has real dimension four, the dimension of $S$.

\emph{(1).} Let $v, v'$ lie in the $+1$ eigenspace of $e_{3}$ on $S$, which is spanned by $p$ and $e_{1}e_{2}p$ ($e_{3}p = p$ and $e_{1}e_{2}$ commutes with $e_{3}$). Then
\[
\langle (\pi v)^{\sim}\,\pi v' \rangle_{0} = \langle \tilde v\,\pi\,v' \rangle_{0} = \tfrac12\langle \tilde v v' \rangle_{0} + \tfrac12\sum_{j} x_{j}\langle \tilde v\,e_{j}\,v' \rangle_{0} = \tfrac12(1 + x_{3})\,\langle \tilde v v' \rangle_{0},
\]
because $e_{1}v'$ and $e_{2}v'$ lie in the $-1$ eigenspace of the symmetric map $e_{3}$, orthogonal to $v$. With $\langle \tilde p\,p \rangle_{0} = \langle (e_{1}e_{2}p)^{\sim}e_{1}e_{2}p \rangle_{0} = \tfrac12$ and $\langle \tilde p\,e_{1}e_{2}\,p \rangle_{0} = 0$ this gives the squares $\tfrac14(1 + x_{3})$ and the orthogonality of $n_{1}, n_{2}$; they lie in $\pi S = G_{+}$, which has rank two, so they are a frame where $x_{3} \neq -1$. The same computation in the $-1$ eigenspace of $e_{3}$, spanned by $e_{1}p$ and $e_{2}p$, gives $s_{1}, s_{2}$ with squares $\tfrac14(1 - x_{3})$. On the equator, $\pi = \pi x$ and $x = \cos a\,e_{1} + \sin a\,e_{2}$, so
\[
\pi e_{1}p = \pi\,x\,e_{1}p = \pi(\cos a + \sin a\,e_{2}e_{1})p = \cos a\,\pi p - \sin a\,\pi e_{1}e_{2}p, \qquad
\pi e_{2}p = \pi\,x\,e_{2}p = \pi(\cos a\,e_{1}e_{2} + \sin a)p = \sin a\,\pi p + \cos a\,\pi e_{1}e_{2}p .
\]

\emph{(2).} $R_{a} = \cos\tfrac a2 + \sin\tfrac a2 f_{1}f_{2} = f_{1}\bigl(\cos\tfrac a2\,f_{1} + \sin\tfrac a2\,f_{2}\bigr)$ is a product of two unit vectors, a rotor in the sense of (L). With this $R_{a}$, $\tilde R_{a} = \cos\tfrac a2 - \sin\tfrac a2 f_{1}f_{2}$, $R_{a}\tilde R_{a} = 1$, and $f_{1}f_{2}$ anticommutes with $f_{1}$ and $f_{2}$ and commutes with every vector orthogonal to both. So $R_{a}f_{1}\tilde R_{a} = R_{a}^{2}f_{1} = (\cos a + \sin a\,f_{1}f_{2})f_{1} = \cos a\,f_{1} - \sin a\,f_{2}$, likewise $R_{a}f_{2}\tilde R_{a} = \sin a\,f_{1} + \cos a\,f_{2}$, and $R_{a}$ fixes the other directions: this is the turn of (1), on the equator $n_{j}$ and $s_{j}$ having the same length. $R_{0} = 1$, $R_{2\pi} = \cos\pi = -1$. On $S^{(k)}$ the frames are $k$ copies of those of (1), mutually orthogonal, the clutching function is the same turn in each of the $k$ planes, and the product of the $k$ commuting rotors $\cos\tfrac a2 + \sin\tfrac a2 f_{2j-1}f_{2j}$ induces it and ends at $(-1)^{k}$.

\emph{(L), the rotors.} In $\Cl(n,0)$ a unit vector has $Q(u) = 1$, so an even versor of unit vectors $R = u_{1}\cdots u_{2j}$ has $R\tilde R = \prod Q(u_{i}) = 1$: $\Spin(n,0) = \Spin^{+}(n,0)$ in the notation of Definition \claimref{obj.std-algebra.pin-spin}, and $\mathrm{SO}^{+}(n,0)$, the products of evenly many reflections with $\prod Q(u_{i}) > 0$, is all of $\mathrm{SO}(n)$. On an even element the twisted adjoint action is $\Ad_{R}(v) = Rv\tilde R$. By Theorem \claimref{std-algebra.spin-double-cover}, $\Ad$ maps the rotors onto $\mathrm{SO}(n)$, is a homomorphism with kernel $\{\pm 1\}$, so $\Ad_{R} = \Ad_{R'}$ exactly when $R' = \pm R$, and maps the versors of unit vectors onto $\mathrm{O}(n)$; it is continuous, being polynomial. \emph{The rotors form a compact set.} Let $\mathcal S$ be the set of even $R$ with $R\tilde R = 1$ such that $Rv\tilde R$ is a vector for every vector $v$. It is closed, and bounded because $\langle \tilde A A \rangle_{0}$ is a positive definite norm on $\Cl(n,0)$ (the sum of the squares of the blade coefficients), in which its elements have length one. Every rotor lies in $\mathcal S$. Conversely let $R \in \mathcal S$. In a finite-dimensional algebra $R\tilde R = 1$ gives $\tilde R R = 1$, so $(Rv\tilde R)^{2} = Rv^{2}\tilde R = Q(v)$: the map $v \mapsto Rv\tilde R$ is an isometry, and by the cited Theorem there is a versor $g$ of unit vectors with $\hat g\,v\,g^{-1} = Rv\tilde R$ for all $v$. Put $y = g^{-1}R$, so that $v\,y = \hat g^{-1}R\,v$. If $g$ is odd, $\hat g = -g$, $y$ is odd and $vy = -yv$ for every vector $v$; expanding $y$ in blades of an orthonormal basis, an odd blade commutes with each basis vector it contains, and conjugation by a basis vector maps each blade to itself up to sign, so no blade of $y$ survives and $y = 0$, impossible since $y$ is invertible (this is the kernel step of the proof of the cited Theorem). So $g$ is even, $y$ is even and commutes with every vector, hence is central, and by \claimref{primer.centre} the even part of the centre is $\R$ (the pseudoscalar, central for $n$ odd, is then odd): $y = \lambda$. Then $1 = R\tilde R = \lambda^{2}g\tilde g = \lambda^{2}$, $R = \pm g$, and $-g$ is again an even versor of unit vectors. So $\mathcal S$ is the set of rotors, which is therefore compact.

\emph{(L), the lifting.} Two consequences of the above. (a) $R$ and $-R$ are at distance $2$ in that norm. (b) For every $\epsilon > 0$ there is $\eta > 0$ such that, if $\Ad_{R}$ and $\Ad_{R'}$ are within $\eta$, then $R'$ is within $\epsilon$ of $R$ or of $-R$: otherwise there are sequences of rotors $R_{j}, R_{j}'$ with $\Ad_{R_{j}} - \Ad_{R_{j}'} \to 0$ and $R_{j}'$ at distance at least $\epsilon$ from $\pm R_{j}$; by compactness they converge along a subsequence to rotors $R, R'$ with $\Ad_{R} = \Ad_{R'}$ and $R' \neq \pm R$, a contradiction.

Take $\eta$ for $\epsilon = \tfrac12$ and, by uniform continuity, $\delta = 1/J$ such that $\kappa$ varies by less than $\eta$ on every square of side $\delta$. \emph{Paths.} Given a continuous path $A(t)$ in $\mathrm{SO}(n)$ varying by less than $\eta$ on intervals of length $\delta$, and a rotor $R_{0}$ over $A(0)$, define $R(t)$ on $[j\delta, (j+1)\delta]$ as the rotor over $A(t)$ within $\tfrac12$ of $R(j\delta)$; by (b) there is one and by (a) only one. It is continuous: for $t'$ near $t$ in the same interval, by (b) with a small $\epsilon'$ the rotor $R(t')$ is within $\epsilon'$ of $R(t)$ or of $-R(t)$, and the second is excluded because $R(t')$ and $R(t)$ are both within $\tfrac12$ of $R(j\delta)$, hence within $1$ of each other, while $-R(t)$ is at distance $2$ from $R(t)$. Two continuous lifts with the same start differ by a continuous sign, so the lift is unique. \emph{The square.} Lift $u \mapsto \kappa(u,0)$ from a rotor over $\kappa(0,0)$ to a path $\rho(u)$, and for each $u$ lift $t \mapsto \kappa(u,t)$ from $\rho(u)$ to $\hat\kappa(u,t)$. The map $\hat\kappa$ is continuous on the square: on the strip $j\delta \leq t \leq (j+1)\delta$, $\hat\kappa(u,t)$ is the rotor over $\kappa(u,t)$ within $\tfrac12$ of $\hat\kappa(u,j\delta)$, and if $\hat\kappa(\cdot, j\delta)$ is continuous then for $(u',t')$ near $(u,t)$ in the strip the rotor $\hat\kappa(u',t')$ is within $\epsilon'$ of $\pm\hat\kappa(u,t)$ and within $\tfrac12 + \tfrac12 + \epsilon'$ of $\hat\kappa(u,t)$, which excludes the minus sign; induction on $j$ starts from the continuity of $\rho$. Since $\kappa(u,1) = \kappa(u,0)$, $\hat\kappa(u,1) = \sigma(u)\,\hat\kappa(u,0)$ with $\sigma(u) = \pm 1$ continuous in $u$, hence constant. At $u = 1$ the path $\kappa(1,\cdot)$ is constant, its lift is constant by uniqueness, and $\sigma(1) = 1$: so $\hat\kappa(u,0) = \hat\kappa(u,1)$ for every $u$ and $\hat\kappa(1,t)$ is independent of $t$. A continuous path of rotors over $\kappa(0,\cdot)$ differs from $\hat\kappa(0,\cdot)$ by a continuous sign, so it is $\pm\hat\kappa(0,\cdot)$ and is closed. This proves (L).

\emph{(3).} Let $k$ be odd and suppose $E = G_{+} \oplus \underline{\R}^{N}$ is trivial over the sphere, $G_{+}$ the positive eigenbundle on $S^{(k)}$, of rank $2k$. $E$ carries the metric of $S^{(k)} \oplus \R^{N}$; a global frame, made orthonormal by the Gram-Schmidt process, which is continuous, gives a global orthonormal frame $\phi$. On the closed hemispheres $D_{N} = \{x_{3} \geq 0\}$ and $D_{S} = \{x_{3} \leq 0\}$ let $\nu$ and $\sigma$ be the orthonormal frames made of the normalised frames of (1), $k$ copies, and the standard basis of $\R^{N}$. Then $\phi = \nu\,\alpha_{N}$ on $D_{N}$ and $\phi = \sigma\,\alpha_{S}$ on $D_{S}$ with continuous $\alpha_{N}, \alpha_{S}$ into $\mathrm{O}(2k + N)$, and on the equator $\sigma = \nu\,\gamma$ with $\gamma(a)$ the turn of (2) in $k$ planes and the identity on the rest. So $\gamma = \alpha_{N}\alpha_{S}^{-1}$ on the equator. For $u, t \in [0,1]$ let $y_{N}(u,t)$ be the point of $D_{N}$ at angular distance $(1-u)\tfrac\pi2$ from the north pole and longitude $2\pi t$, $y_{S}(u,t)$ its mirror image in the equatorial plane, and
\[
c(u,t) = \alpha_{N}\bigl(y_{N}(u,t)\bigr)\,\alpha_{S}\bigl(y_{S}(u,t)\bigr)^{-1} .
\]
It is continuous, $c(u,0) = c(u,1)$, $c(1,t)$ is constant (the poles), and $c(0,t) = \gamma(2\pi t)$. Its determinant is continuous with values $\pm 1$ and equals $1$ at $c(0,0) = \gamma(0) = 1$, so $c$ maps into $\mathrm{SO}(2k + N)$. By (2) the rotor path $R(t)$, the product of the $k$ plane rotors at $a = 2\pi t$, is a continuous lift of $c(0,\cdot)$ with $R(0) = 1$ and $R(1) = (-1)^{k} = -1$. This contradicts (L), applied with $\kappa = c$ and $n = 2k + N$. So $G_{+} \oplus \underline{\R}^{N}$ is not trivial. The bundle $G_{-}$ is the pull-back of $G_{+}$ by the antipodal map $x \mapsto -x$, so a trivialisation of $G_{-} \oplus \underline{\R}^{N}$ would pull back to one of $G_{+} \oplus \underline{\R}^{N}$.

\emph{(4).} Let $h$ be a model completion standard outside the bounded set $U$, nondegenerate at every point of $\R^{3}$, with exterior form $K_{0}$ on $W_{0}$. By clause (4) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.strict-completions-exist-exactly-when-the-signature-does-not-jump}, the base being contractible, $G_{+} \oplus (K_{0})_{+}$ is trivial on $\R^{3} \setminus U$. Choose $r$ with $U$ inside the ball of radius $r$. On the sphere of radius $r$ the positive eigenbundle of $g(x)$ is that of $g(x/r)$, the bundle $G_{+}$ of the unit sphere, and $(K_{0})_{+}$ is a fixed subspace, of dimension $N$ say. So $G_{+} \oplus \underline{\R}^{N}$ is trivial over the sphere, against (3). Strict completions: the signature of $G$ is $(2k,2k)$ at every point other than the origin, so clause (3) of that Theorem applies and the double is one; its $K = -G$ has $K_{\pm} = G_{\mp}$.

\emph{(5).} In $\Cl(4,0)$, $(e_{1}e_{2}e_{3}e_{4})^{2} = 1$, so $p_{4}$ is an idempotent, and $T = \Cl(4,0)p_{4}$ has dimension eight (computed). """The position vector on the least module of Cl(3,0): clutching function and rotor lift, exact.

The least module is the left ideal S = Cl(3,0) p, p = (1 + e3)/2, of dimension four, with the product
<psi~ phi>_0 (scalar part); multiplication by a vector x on the left is symmetric for it and squares to Q(x).
Over the unit sphere the positive eigenbundle is G_+ = { (x, psi) : x psi = psi } = pi(x) S, pi(x) = (1 + x)/2.

(1) Generators: e1, e2, e3 act on S by symmetric anticommuting maps of square one; g(x)^2 = Q(x).
(2) Frames: pi(x) p, pi(x) e1e2 p are orthogonal of square (1 + x3)/4 each (a frame where x3 > -1);
    pi(x) e1 p, pi(x) e2 p are orthogonal of square (1 - x3)/4 each (a frame where x3 < 1).
(3) Clutching: at x = (c, s, 0) the second frame is the first turned by the angle of x:
    pi e1 p = c pi p - s pi e1e2 p,  pi e2 p = s pi p + c pi e1e2 p.  One full turn round the equator.
(4) Rotor lift: in Cl(2 + N, 0) the rotor R = cos(a/2) + sin(a/2) f1f2 turns the frame (f1, f2) as in (3),
    R f1 R~ = c f1 - s f2, R f2 R~ = s f1 + c f2, and fixes the other directions; along the turn it runs from 1
    to -1. For k planes turned together it ends at (-1)^k.
(5) Two copies: the least module of Cl(4,0), the ideal T = Cl(4,0) p4, p4 = (1 + e1e2e3e4)/2, of dimension eight,
    is S p4 + S e1 p4 under Cl(3,0), two orthogonal copies of S (the product halved), and e4 is a fourth symmetric
    anticommuting generator: (x + b e4)^2 = Q(x) + b^2.
(6) On S itself no fourth symmetric map anticommutes with e1, e2, e3.
(7) For the lifting clause (L): in Cl(n,0), n = 1..6, the only even blade commuting with every basis vector is
    the scalar, and no odd blade anticommutes with every basis vector (conjugation by a basis vector is diagonal
    on blades, so this decides it for all elements); the plane rotor is a product of two unit vectors.
"""
from fractions import Fraction as F

import GA
from tp_premise import premise

SQ3 = GA.sig(3, 0)
SQ4 = GA.sig(4, 0)
N_EXTRA = 3                      # trivial directions added in the rotor check
SQF = GA.sig(2 + N_EXTRA, 0)     # fibre algebra of the stabilised bundle
SQK = GA.sig(6, 0)               # three planes, for k = 1, 2, 3 copies

# rational points of the circle, (c, s) with c^2 + s^2 = 1, from (a, b): c = (a^2-b^2)/(a^2+b^2), s = 2ab/(a^2+b^2)
CIRCLE_SEEDS = [(1, 0), (2, 1), (1, 1), (1, 2), (0, 1), (-1, 2), (-1, 1), (-2, 1), (3, 2), (-3, 5), (5, -1), (1, -3)]
# rational points of the sphere from (u, v): x = (2u, 2v, u^2+v^2-1)/(u^2+v^2+1), and the two poles
SPHERE_SEEDS = [(0, 0), (1, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1), (2, -1), (F(1, 2), F(1, 3)), (-3, 2), (F(-2, 5), 4), (7, 7)]
# the turn in N_STEPS + 1 points: half-angle parameters (1 - j/N_STEPS, j/N_STEPS)
N_STEPS = 12
SAMPLE_VECTORS = [(1, 0, 0), (0, 1, 0), (0, 0, 1), (2, -1, 3), (F(1, 2), F(2, 3), -5), (0, 0, 0), (-4, 4, 1)]
SAMPLE_COUPLINGS = [F(0), F(1), F(-2, 3), F(5, 7)]
CENTRE_DIMENSIONS = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]


def circle_point(a, b):
    a, b = F(a), F(b)
    d = a * a + b * b
    return (a * a - b * b) / d, 2 * a * b / d


def sphere_point(u, v):
    u, v = F(u), F(v)
    d = u * u + v * v + 1
    return 2 * u / d, 2 * v / d, (u * u + v * v - 1) / d


def vec(x, n=3):
    out = {}
    for i in range(n):
        if i < len(x) and x[i] != 0:
            out[(i,)] = F(x[i])
    return out


def blade(*idx):
    return {tuple(idx): F(1)}


def pair(a, b, squares):
    """<a~ b>_0."""
    return GA.mul(GA.reverse(a), b, squares).get((), F(0))


P3 = GA.scal(F(1, 2), GA.add(GA.sc(1), GA.gen(2)))                    # p = (1 + e3)/2
IDEAL3 = [P3, GA.mul(GA.gen(0), P3, SQ3), GA.mul(GA.gen(1), P3, SQ3), GA.mul(blade(0, 1), P3, SQ3)]
BLADES3 = GA.all_blades(3)
BLADES4 = GA.all_blades(4)


def coords(psi, basis, blades):
    """Coordinates of psi in a list of independent multivectors (exact solve), or None."""
    rows = [GA.basis_vector_of(b, blades) for b in basis]
    target = GA.basis_vector_of(psi, blades)
    n = len(basis)
    # solve sum_j c_j rows[j] = target by elimination on the transposed system
    m = [[rows[j][i] for j in range(n)] + [target[i]] for i in range(len(blades))]
    piv_cols, r = [], 0
    for col in range(n):
        piv = next((i for i in range(r, len(m)) if m[i][col] != 0), None)
        if piv is None:
            return None
        m[r], m[piv] = m[piv], m[r]
        pv = m[r][col]
        m[r] = [a / pv for a in m[r]]
        for i in range(len(m)):
            if i != r and m[i][col] != 0:
                f = m[i][col]
                m[i] = [a - f * b for a, b in zip(m[i], m[r])]
        piv_cols.append(col)
        r += 1
    if any(row[n] != 0 for row in m[r:]):
        return None
    return [m[i][n] for i in range(n)]


def left_matrix(a, basis, blades, squares):
    """Matrix of psi -> a psi on the span of basis (columns are images)."""
    cols = [coords(GA.mul(a, b, squares), basis, blades) for b in basis]
    if any(c is None for c in cols):
        return None
    n = len(basis)
    return [[cols[j][i] for j in range(n)] for i in range(n)]


def gram(basis, squares):
    return [[pair(a, b, squares) for b in basis] for a in basis]


def is_symmetric_for(m, g):
    """m^T g = g m."""
    n = len(m)
    mt = [[m[j][i] for j in range(n)] for i in range(n)]
    return GA.mat_eq(GA.mat_mul(mt, g), GA.mat_mul(g, m))


def check_least_module_and_symmetric_generators():
    premise("std-algebra.periodicity")
    ok = True
    # p is an idempotent and the ideal has dimension four, half of Cl(3,0)
    ok = ok and GA.eq(GA.mul(P3, P3, SQ3), P3)
    ok = ok and GA.rank_of_vectors([GA.basis_vector_of(b, BLADES3) for b in IDEAL3]) == 4
    ok = ok and len(BLADES3) == 8
    g = gram(IDEAL3, SQ3)
    ok = ok and GA.congruence_signature(g) == (4, 0, 0)
    mats = [left_matrix(GA.gen(i), IDEAL3, BLADES3, SQ3) for i in range(3)]
    ok = ok and all(m is not None for m in mats)
    ident = [[F(1) if i == j else F(0) for j in range(4)] for i in range(4)]
    zero = [[F(0)] * 4 for _ in range(4)]
    for i in range(3):
        ok = ok and is_symmetric_for(mats[i], g)
        ok = ok and GA.mat_eq(GA.mat_mul(mats[i], mats[i]), ident)
        for j in range(i + 1, 3):
            ac = [[a + b for a, b in zip(r1, r2)] for r1, r2 in
                  zip(GA.mat_mul(mats[i], mats[j]), GA.mat_mul(mats[j], mats[i]))]
            ok = ok and GA.mat_eq(ac, zero)
    # g(x)^2 = Q(x) on the module, for sample vectors: degenerate exactly at x = 0
    for x in SAMPLE_VECTORS:
        xv = vec(x)
        q = sum(F(c) * F(c) for c in x)
        for b in IDEAL3:
            ok = ok and GA.eq(GA.mul(xv, GA.mul(xv, b, SQ3), SQ3), GA.scal(q, b))
        m = left_matrix(xv, IDEAL3, BLADES3, SQ3) if xv else zero
        gm = GA.mat_mul(g, m)
        sig = GA.congruence_signature(gm)
        ok = ok and (sig == (2, 2, 0) if q != 0 else sig == (0, 0, 4))
    GA.check("the ideal Cl(3,0)(1+e3)/2 has dimension four; e1, e2, e3 act on it by symmetric anticommuting maps of "
             "square one; g(x)^2 = Q(x), the form of g(x) has signature (2,2) for x != 0 and vanishes at x = 0", ok)
    return ok


def frames(x):
    """North and south frames of the positive eigenbundle at the unit vector x."""
    pi = GA.scal(F(1, 2), GA.add(GA.sc(1), vec(x)))
    north = [GA.mul(pi, IDEAL3[0], SQ3), GA.mul(pi, IDEAL3[3], SQ3)]
    south = [GA.mul(pi, IDEAL3[1], SQ3), GA.mul(pi, IDEAL3[2], SQ3)]
    return pi, north, south


def check_hemisphere_frames_of_the_positive_eigenbundle():
    ok = True
    pts = [sphere_point(u, v) for (u, v) in SPHERE_SEEDS] + [(F(0), F(0), F(1))]
    for x in pts:
        ok = ok and sum(c * c for c in x) == 1
        pi, north, south = frames(x)
        xv = vec(x)
        for f in north + south:
            ok = ok and GA.eq(GA.mul(xv, f, SQ3), f)              # in the +1 eigenspace
        gn, gs = gram(north, SQ3), gram(south, SQ3)
        ok = ok and gn == [[(1 + x[2]) / 4, F(0)], [F(0), (1 + x[2]) / 4]]
        ok = ok and gs == [[(1 - x[2]) / 4, F(0)], [F(0), (1 - x[2]) / 4]]
        # the eigenspace has dimension two
        allf = [GA.mul(pi, b, SQ3) for b in IDEAL3]
        ok = ok and GA.rank_of_vectors([GA.basis_vector_of(f, BLADES3) for f in allf]) == 2
    # the poles: the north frame vanishes at the south pole only, the south frame at the north pole only
    south_pole, north_pole = (F(0), F(0), F(-1)), (F(0), F(0), F(1))
    ok = ok and all(GA.is_zero(f) for f in frames(south_pole)[1])
    ok = ok and all(GA.is_zero(f) for f in frames(north_pole)[2])
    ok = ok and not any(GA.is_zero(f) for f in frames(north_pole)[1])
    GA.check("pi(x) p, pi(x) e1e2 p are orthogonal of square (1+x3)/4 and pi(x) e1 p, pi(x) e2 p orthogonal of "
             "square (1-x3)/4 at ten rational points of the sphere; the eigenspace has dimension two", ok)
    return ok


def check_clutching_function_is_one_full_turn():
    ok = True
    turned = []
    for (a, b) in CIRCLE_SEEDS:
        c, s = circle_point(a, b)
        ok = ok and c * c + s * s == 1
        pi, north, south = frames((c, s, F(0)))
        # south_j = sum_i north_i gamma_ij with gamma = [[c, s], [-s, c]]
        ok = ok and GA.eq(south[0], GA.add(GA.scal(c, north[0]), GA.scal(-s, north[1])))
        ok = ok and GA.eq(south[1], GA.add(GA.scal(s, north[0]), GA.scal(c, north[1])))
        turned.append((c, s))
    # the angle of gamma is the angle of x: the points visit all four open quadrants and the axes
    quad = {(c > 0, s > 0) for (c, s) in turned if c != 0 and s != 0}
    ok = ok and len(quad) == 4 and (F(1), F(0)) in turned and (F(-1), F(0)) in turned
    # the turn is not a turn of the frame through twice the angle: at x = (0, 1, 0) gamma = [[0, 1], [-1, 0]]
    c, s = circle_point(1, 1)
    pi, north, south = frames((c, s, F(0)))
    ok = ok and (c, s) == (0, 1) and GA.eq(south[0], GA.neg(north[1])) and GA.eq(south[1], north[0])
    GA.check("on the equator x = (c, s, 0) the south frame is the north frame turned by the angle of x, "
             "gamma = [[c, s], [-s, c]], at twelve rational points in all four quadrants: one full turn", ok)
    return ok


def plane_rotor(ch, sh, i, j):
    """cos(a/2) + sin(a/2) f_i f_j."""
    return GA.add(GA.sc(ch), GA.scal(sh, blade(i, j)))


def check_rotor_lift_of_the_full_turn_ends_at_minus_one():
    premise("std-algebra.spin-double-cover")
    ok = True
    path = []
    for j in range(N_STEPS + 1):
        a, b = F(N_STEPS - j, N_STEPS), F(j, N_STEPS)
        ch, sh = circle_point(a, b)                    # half angle t/2 from 0 to pi
        c, s = ch * ch - sh * sh, 2 * ch * sh           # the angle t from 0 to 2 pi
        r = plane_rotor(ch, sh, 0, 1)
        ok = ok and GA.eq(GA.mul(r, GA.reverse(r), SQF), GA.sc(1))
        # R f_j R~ = sum_i f_i gamma_ij with gamma = [[c, s], [-s, c]], the clutching function; the rest fixed
        img = [GA.mul(GA.mul(r, GA.gen(i), SQF), GA.reverse(r), SQF) for i in range(2 + N_EXTRA)]
        ok = ok and GA.eq(img[0], GA.add(GA.scal(c, GA.gen(0)), GA.scal(-s, GA.gen(1))))
        ok = ok and GA.eq(img[1], GA.add(GA.scal(s, GA.gen(0)), GA.scal(c, GA.gen(1))))
        ok = ok and all(GA.eq(img[i], GA.gen(i)) for i in range(2, 2 + N_EXTRA))
        path.append((c, s, r))
    # the loop of rotations is closed, its lift is not: it runs from 1 to -1
    ok = ok and path[0][:2] == (1, 0) and path[-1][:2] == (1, 0)
    ok = ok and GA.eq(path[0][2], GA.sc(1)) and GA.eq(path[-1][2], GA.sc(-1))
    # consecutive lifts are the nearer of the two preimages: <R_j~ R_{j+1}>_0 > 0
    ok = ok and all(pair(path[j][2], path[j + 1][2], SQF) > 0 for j in range(N_STEPS))
    # k planes turned together (k copies of the module): the lift ends at (-1)^k
    for k in (1, 2, 3):
        ends = []
        for (a, b) in [(1, 0), (0, 1)]:
            ch, sh = circle_point(a, b)
            r = GA.sc(1)
            for q in range(k):
                r = GA.mul(r, plane_rotor(ch, sh, 2 * q, 2 * q + 1), SQK)
            ends.append(r)
        ok = ok and GA.eq(ends[0], GA.sc(1)) and GA.eq(ends[1], GA.sc((-1) ** k))
    GA.check("the rotor cos(a/2) + sin(a/2) f1f2 turns the frame plane by the clutching angle and fixes three "
             "added directions; along the full turn it runs from 1 to -1 in thirteen steps, each the nearer "
             "preimage; for k planes turned together it ends at (-1)^k, k = 1, 2, 3", ok)
    return ok


def check_two_copies_carry_a_fourth_generator():
    premise("std-algebra.periodicity")
    premise("synthesis.strict-completions-exist-exactly-when-the-signature-does-not-jump")
    ok = True
    omega = blade(0, 1, 2, 3)
    ok = ok and GA.eq(GA.mul(omega, omega, SQ4), GA.sc(1))
    p4 = GA.scal(F(1, 2), GA.add(GA.sc(1), omega))
    ok = ok and GA.eq(GA.mul(p4, p4, SQ4), p4)
    cand = [GA.mul({b: F(1)}, p4, SQ4) for b in BLADES4]
    vecs = [GA.basis_vector_of(c, BLADES4) for c in cand]
    ok = ok and GA.rank_of_vectors(vecs) == 8
    basis, rows = [], []
    for c, v in zip(cand, vecs):
        if GA.rank_of_vectors(rows + [v]) == len(rows) + 1:
            basis.append(c)
            rows.append(v)
    ok = ok and len(basis) == 8
    g = gram(basis, SQ4)
    ok = ok and GA.congruence_signature(g) == (8, 0, 0)
    mats = [left_matrix(GA.gen(i), basis, BLADES4, SQ4) for i in range(4)]
    ident = [[F(1) if i == j else F(0) for j in range(8)] for i in range(8)]
    zero = [[F(0)] * 8 for _ in range(8)]
    for i in range(4):
        ok = ok and mats[i] is not None and is_symmetric_for(mats[i], g)
        ok = ok and GA.mat_eq(GA.mat_mul(mats[i], mats[i]), ident)
        for j in range(i + 1, 4):
            ac = [[a + b for a, b in zip(r1, r2)] for r1, r2 in
                  zip(GA.mat_mul(mats[i], mats[j]), GA.mat_mul(mats[j], mats[i]))]
            ok = ok and GA.mat_eq(ac, zero)
    # under Cl(3,0) it is two copies of S: s -> s p4 and s -> s e1 p4 are module maps (right multiplications),
    # each injective and a multiple of an isometry, with orthogonal images that span the ideal
    lift3 = [{k: v for k, v in b.items()} for b in IDEAL3]
    copy1 = [GA.mul(b, p4, SQ4) for b in lift3]
    copy2 = [GA.mul(GA.mul(b, GA.gen(0), SQ4), p4, SQ4) for b in lift3]
    g3 = gram(IDEAL3, SQ3)
    half = [[x / 2 for x in row] for row in g3]
    ok = ok and gram(copy1, SQ4) == half and gram(copy2, SQ4) == half
    ok = ok and all(pair(a, b, SQ4) == 0 for a in copy1 for b in copy2)
    ok = ok and GA.rank_of_vectors([GA.basis_vector_of(c, BLADES4) for c in copy1 + copy2]) == 8
    for i in range(3):
        for b3, c1, c2 in zip(IDEAL3, copy1, copy2):
            eb = GA.mul(GA.gen(i), b3, SQ3)
            ok = ok and GA.eq(GA.mul(GA.gen(i), c1, SQ4), GA.mul(eb, p4, SQ4))
            ok = ok and GA.eq(GA.mul(GA.gen(i), c2, SQ4), GA.mul(GA.mul(eb, GA.gen(0), SQ4), p4, SQ4))
    for x in SAMPLE_VECTORS:
        for bcoup in SAMPLE_COUPLINGS:
            y = GA.add(vec(x, 4), GA.scal(bcoup, GA.gen(3)))
            q = sum(F(c) * F(c) for c in x) + bcoup * bcoup
            for b in basis[:3]:
                ok = ok and GA.eq(GA.mul(y, GA.mul(y, b, SQ4), SQ4), GA.scal(q, b))
            if y:
                m = left_matrix(y, basis, BLADES4, SQ4)
                sig = GA.congruence_signature(GA.mat_mul(g, m))
                ok = ok and sig == (4, 4, 0)
    GA.check("the ideal Cl(4,0)(1+e1e2e3e4)/2 has dimension eight and is two orthogonal copies of the least module "
             "of Cl(3,0); e1..e4 act by symmetric anticommuting maps of square one; (x + b e4)^2 = Q(x) + b^2 and "
             "the form has signature (4,4) unless x = 0 and b = 0", ok)
    return ok


def check_no_fourth_generator_on_the_least_module():
    premise("synthesis.strict-completions-exist-exactly-when-the-signature-does-not-jump")
    ok = True
    g = gram(IDEAL3, SQ3)
    mats = [left_matrix(GA.gen(i), IDEAL3, BLADES3, SQ3) for i in range(3)]
    n = 4
    # unknown X (16 entries); equations X E_i + E_i X = 0 (i = 1, 2, 3) and X^T g - g X = 0
    rows = []
    for m in mats:
        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(n):
                row = [F(0)] * (n * n)
                for k in range(n):
                    row[i * n + k] += m[k][j]          # (X m)_ij
                    row[k * n + j] += m[i][k]          # (m X)_ij
                rows.append(row)
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(n):
            row = [F(0)] * (n * n)
            for k in range(n):
                row[k * n + i] += g[k][j]              # (X^T g)_ij
                row[k * n + j] -= g[i][k]              # (g X)_ij
            rows.append(row)
    ok = ok and GA.rank_of_vectors(rows) == n * n      # only X = 0
    # without the symmetry condition the anticommuting maps form a plane (the antisymmetric ones)
    ok = ok and GA.rank_of_vectors(rows[:3 * n * n]) == n * n - 2
    GA.check("on the least module of Cl(3,0) no nonzero symmetric map anticommutes with e1, e2, e3 "
             "(the anticommuting maps form a plane of antisymmetric ones)", ok)
    return ok


def check_elements_commuting_or_anticommuting_with_every_vector():
    premise("primer.centre")
    premise("std-algebra.spin-double-cover")
    ok = True
    for n in CENTRE_DIMENSIONS:
        squares = GA.sig(n, 0)
        even_central, odd_anti = [], []
        for b in GA.all_blades(n):
            x = {b: F(1)}
            signs = []
            for i in range(n):

                # conjugation by a basis vector is diagonal on blades: e x = +- x e

                even_central.append(b)
            if len(b) % 2 == 1 and all(sg == -1 for sg in signs):
                odd_anti.append(b)
        ok = ok and even_central == [()] and odd_anti == []
    # the plane rotor is a product of two unit vectors: cos(a/2) + sin(a/2) f1f2 = f1 (cos(a/2) f1 + sin(a/2) f2)
    for (a, b) in CIRCLE_SEEDS:
        ch, sh = circle_point(a, b)
        u = GA.add(GA.scal(ch, GA.gen(0)), GA.scal(sh, GA.gen(1)))
        ok = ok and GA.eq(GA.mul(u, u, SQF), GA.sc(1))
        ok = ok and GA.eq(GA.mul(GA.gen(0), u, SQF), plane_rotor(ch, sh, 0, 1))
    GA.check("in Cl(n,0), n = 1..6: conjugation by a basis vector is diagonal on blades, the only even blade "
             "commuting with every basis vector is the scalar and no odd blade anticommutes with all of them; "
             "the plane rotor is a product of two unit vectors", ok)
    return ok
